properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 28 at 8:58AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent gusty northeast winds and upstream tidal effects are
slowing river flow on the St Johns River at Astor. River levels are
forecast to begin a slow decline late this week, but remain in
Moderate Flood stage for at least the next couple weeks.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland, Astor...Moderate flooding
is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 3.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...River levels are forecast to crest around 3.8 feet
this week, then begin a gradual decline late in the week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 200 AM EDT.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 28 at 2:56AM HST until October 29 at 5:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
A trough moving over the state is bringing abundant tropical
moisture expected to last though this evening. Heavy rain and
isolated thunderstorms are expected to produce flash flooding, and
while the greatest flood threat will be focused over Oahu and Maui
County, all islands are at risk.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...All main Hawaiian Islands.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Significant flooding may occur due to the overflow of
streams and drainages. Roads in several areas may be closed, along
with property damage in urban or low lying spots due to runoff.
Landslides may also occur in areas with steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms with intense rain rates
may develop at any time through tonight as a trough continues
moving over the state. While the greatest flood threat will be
focused over Oahu and Maui County, all islands are at risk.
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The island of Oahu in Honolulu County...

* WHEN...Until 415 AM HST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding on roads, poor drainage areas, and in
streams. River or stream flows are elevated. Ponding of water in
urban or other areas is occurring or is imminent.

a band of heavy rain over eastern Oahu will continue to move
eastward into the Kaiwi Channel over the next hour. Rain was
falling at a rate of up to 1 inches per hour. Minor flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory area.

Honolulu, Maunawili, Manoa, Palolo, Waimanalo, Kailua, Kaneohe,
Hawaii Kai, Kalihi, Kaneohe Marine Base, Ahuimanu and Moanalua.

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 28 at 3:46AM AKDT until October 28 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Water levels of 1 to 2 feet above the normal highest
tide line.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM AKDT today, highest water levels expected
during each upcoming high tide through this morning.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas. Coastal
erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Steady south to southwesterly flow is
expected to continue for the Kuskokwim Delta coastline through
this morning. Coastal erosion and perhaps nuisance flooding of
low-lying areas will be possible with high tide due to the
persistent onshore winds. Possible maximum water levels of
between 1 and 2 ft above the normal highest tide line, including
in and around Kipnuk and Kwigillingok. A brief break in winds
and thus, elevated water levels occurs late today, but a second
round of elevated water levels and persistent southerly winds
are forecast with the arrival of yet another front late Thursday
into Friday.
properties.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

NWSheadline: HIGH SURF ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 AM AKDT THIS MORNING
